The slide features a large bold title 'Negative Prompting' at the top-left, followed by a sub-heading stating the intuition behind the method. The central content is a horizontal diagram showing the processing of an image of a cat. On the left, the original image is connected via two colored arrows (teal for 'std. prompt' and yellow for 'neg. prompt') to two corresponding heatmaps in the center. Speech bubbles above and below the arrows contain the text prompts 'a photo of a cat' and 'the background of a cat'. To the right of the heatmaps, there is a comparison grid with two columns titled 'CLIP' and 'Ours'. This grid contains bar charts representing activation levels; the top row shows both methods succeeding (green checkmarks), while the bottom row shows CLIP failing (red 'X') and the proposed method succeeding (green checkmark). At the bottom of the slide, a 'Strategy' statement is written in a large font. A small circular video inset of the presenter is visible in the bottom-right corner.

The slide features a large, bold title 'Negative Prompting' at the top-left, followed by a sub-heading 'Intuition: Different prompts activates distinct pixel areas'. The central content is a diagram illustrating the concept. On the left, an image of a cat is shown with two speech bubbles: a teal one for 'a photo of a cat' (standard prompt) and an orange one for 'the background of a cat' (negative prompt). Two colored arrows point from these prompts to corresponding heatmap visualizations of the cat image. To the right of the heatmaps is a 2x2 grid of bar charts comparing 'CLIP' and 'Ours'. The 'CLIP' column shows a green checkmark for the standard prompt but a red 'X' for the negative prompt, while the 'Ours' column shows green checkmarks for both. At the bottom, a summary statement 'Strategy: Enforce the model to "ignore" such negative prompts which activate the spurious correlations' is displayed in bold. A small circular inset in the bottom-right corner shows the presenter's video feed.

The slide features a large, complex architectural diagram titled 'Method Overview' in a serif font at the top-left. The diagram is organized into three main sections labeled (a), (b), and (c), each enclosed in dashed-line boxes. Section (a) at the top-left illustrates the generation of 'Attribute Candidates' from a class name ('Bobolink') using an LLM with specific templates. Section (b) at the top-center shows these attributes and an image being processed by text and image encoders for 'Attribute Clustering' and subsequent 'Attribute Sampling'. Section (c) occupies the entire bottom half, detailing the training process involving 'Soft Prompts', 'Textural Prompting', and multiple loss functions (L_ent, L_reg, L_neg) connecting text and image encoder outputs. A 'Notations' legend is positioned on the far right, defining visual symbols like learnable tokens and gradient paths. The overall text density is moderate, primarily consisting of labels and mathematical notation within the flowchart. A small video inset of the presenter is located in the bottom-right corner.

The slide features a large, complex architectural diagram titled 'Method Overview' in a bold serif font at the top-left. The content is organized into three main sub-sections labeled (a), (b), and (c), each enclosed within dashed-line boundaries. Section (a) at the top-left shows the input 'Bobolink' class and image being processed by an LLM to generate attribute candidates. Section (b) at the top-right illustrates attribute clustering and sampling using frozen text and image encoders. Section (c) spans the bottom half of the slide, detailing the core methodology involving soft prompts, textural prompting, and a training loop with multiple loss functions ($L_{ent}$, $L_{reg}$, $L_{neg}$). A 'Notations' legend is located on the far right, defining visual symbols like red dashed arrows for gradients and various colored circles for different token types. The diagram uses a color palette of green, blue, and orange for different modules. A small circular inset video of the presenter is positioned in the bottom-right corner.
